chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān wrote to al-Riḍā عليه السلام:

I had ten dirhams owed to me by a man, and the ruler invalidated those dirhams and brought dirhams higher than those dirhams in value. And in those first dirhams today there is depreciation. So what is due to me from him: the first dirhams which the ruler invalidated, or the dirhams which the ruler approved?
So he wrote: “You are entitled to the first dirhams.”

key_terms.السُّلْطَانَ: the ruling authority who invalidated one currency and approved another
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: dirhams, the monetary units in which the debt was owed

ai.seo_question: If old dirhams were invalidated and replaced, is a debt repaid according to the original dirhams or the new currency?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling regarding a debt denominated in dirhams after the ruler withdrew the old currency and introduced a higher-valued one. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام ruled that the creditor is entitled to the original dirhams, indicating that the debt remains tied to the original monetary denomination.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3716 - Yunus ibn Abdul Rahman wrote to Al-Ridha (as), saying:

"I had ten dirhams owed to me by a man, but the ruler invalidated those dirhams and introduced new dirhams that are higher in value than the previous ones. The earlier dirhams are now devalued. What is my right upon him-the original dirhams that the ruler invalidated or the new dirhams approved by the ruler?"
Imam (as) wrote in response: "You have the right to the original dirhams."
